布朗运动与扩散 · 3D 互动课件: Brownian Motion and Diffusion · 3D Interactive Lesson
选择性必修第三册 · 第一章第一节（印刷页 p.3–6）: Elective Required Book 3 · Ch. 1 Sec. 1 (printed pp.3–6)
看不见的分子，凭什么说它在乱动？: Molecules are invisible, so how do we know they're moving randomly?
显微镜下，悬浮的小炭粒在自己的位置附近无规则游走: Under a microscope, suspended carbon particles wander randomly around their positions
每 30 s 记一个点，连成的折线不是它的真实路径: One point every 30 s; the zigzag line joining them is not the real path
液体分子四面撞它、撞击不平衡，微粒才改变运动状态: Liquid molecules hit it from all sides; unbalanced impacts change its motion
微粒越小、温度越高，运动越明显（撞击数变少、η 变小）: The smaller the particle and the higher the temperature, the more pronounced the motion (fewer impacts, smaller η)
同一个根源（分子热运动），让浓度从高向低展开: The same root cause (molecular thermal motion) spreads concentration from high to low
高倍显微镜 + 载玻片 + 稀释墨汁，结果由显示器呈现（教材 p.3）: High-power microscope + slide + diluted ink, results shown on a monitor (textbook p.3)
每 30 s 记一个位置，用线段依次连成折线（教材图 1.1-4）: Record a position every 30 s and join them in order with line segments (textbook Fig. 1.1-4)
炭粒被四面撞来的分子推着乱走（已放大绘制）: The carbon particle is pushed around by molecules hitting it from all sides (drawn enlarged)
静水里滴一滴墨，浓度从高向低展开: A drop of ink in still water; concentration spreads from high to low
显微镜下，小炭粒为什么会自己动起来？: Under the microscope, why does a small carbon particle move on its own?
在 3D 里点一下前右侧那台显示器，把悬浊液的视野打开: In 3D, click the monitor at the front right to open the view of the suspension
显示器上出现一片浑浊的视野，几颗小黑点各自乱走、方向随时在变；水没有流动，也没有: A cloudy field of view appears on the monitor, with several small black dots each wandering about, changing direction all the time; the water isn't flowing and nobody is stirring it. The lens is at 1 000× (the textbook uses 400× or 1 000×).
悬浮在液体中的微粒做无规则的、不停息的运动，这就是布朗运动；1827 年布朗首先: Particles suspended in a liquid move randomly and ceaselessly; this is Brownian motion, first studied under a microscope by Brown in 1827. The particles are too small for the naked eye, so a high-power microscope is needed, and the results can be shown on a monitor (textbook pp.3–4).
A2.3、A4.1、A6.1（人教选必3 · 印刷页 p.3–4）: A2.3, A4.1, A6.1 (PEP Elective Book 3 · printed pp.3–4)
看到的是悬浮的微粒（约 10⁻⁶ m 级），不是分子——分子约 0.1 nm 级: What you see are suspended particles (on the order of 10⁻⁶ m), not molecules; molecules are on the order of 0.1 nm, far beyond what an optical microscope can resolve; the particles' motion is only indirect evidence of molecular impacts (textbook p.4 margin note).
必须用高倍显微镜：教材演示调至 400 倍或 1 000 倍，目镜里的结果可以通: A high-power microscope is needed: the textbook demonstration uses 400× or 1 000×, and what's seen in the eyepiece can be shown on a monitor (p.3).
没有定向漂移：它东一步、西一步，方向随时在变，不是被水流冲着走。: There's no steady drift: it steps one way, then another, changing direction constantly, not carried along by a current.
去掉这一步：学生会把布朗运动当成「分子自己在动」或「水把微粒冲着走」。: Skip this step and students treat Brownian motion as "molecules moving on their own" or "water carrying the particles along".
常考：布朗运动是悬浮微粒的运动，不是分子的运动（教材 p.6 第 3 题 (1): Often tested: Brownian motion is the motion of suspended particles, not of molecules (textbook p.6 question 3 (1)(2)).
布朗运动 = 悬浮微粒的无规则运动: Brownian motion = random motion of suspended particles
把它的位置每 30 秒记一次，连起来是什么样子？: Record its position every 30 seconds and join the points: what does it look like?
把「记录次数」从 4 次拖到 10 次：方格纸上每 30 s 记一个点，看折线怎: Drag "Number of records" from 4 to 10: one point is recorded on the grid every 30 s; watch the zigzag line grow
方格纸上出现 10 个记录点、9 段折线：从起点到第 10 点的净位移 16.5: 10 recorded points and 9 segments appear on the grid: the net displacement from start to point 10 is 16.50 μm, while the zigzag covers 64.8 μm in total, and the mean squared displacement is 512.3 μm².
每隔 30 s 记下一个位置，再用线段按时间顺序连起来，就得到教材图 1.1-4: Record a position every 30 s and join them in time order with line segments to get a zigzag like textbook Fig. 1.1-4. The zigzag isn't the real path; textbook p.4 says it clearly: "even within 30 s, the particle's motion is extremely irregular".
A4.4、A6.2（教材 p.4 图 1.1-4）、A5.4、B2.2 表 1: A4.4, A6.2 (textbook p.4 Fig. 1.1-4), A5.4, B2.2 table 1 ①
记录间隔 30 s 是教材给的值（p.4），不是「微粒每 30 s 才动一下」。: The 30 s recording interval is the textbook's value (p.4), not "the particle only moves every 30 s".
折线只是采样连线：两个记录点之间，微粒照样在乱走（放大视窗里能看到那段锯齿）。: The zigzag only joins samples: between two recorded points the particle keeps wandering (the jagged path is visible in the magnified window).
净位移 16.50 μm 远小于路程 64.8 μm——它东一步西一步，大部分互: The net displacement of 16.50 μm is far less than the path length of 64.8 μm; it steps one way then another, and most steps cancel out.
去掉这一步：学生会把折线当真实路径（教材 p.6 第 4 题「小李」的错误）。: Skip this step and students take the zigzag as the real path (the mistake of "Xiao Li" in textbook p.6 question 4).
常考：折线是每隔 30 s 的位置连线，不是真实轨迹（教材 p.6 第 4 题）: Often tested: the zigzag joins positions every 30 s and is not the real trajectory (textbook p.6 question 4).
记录时间从 2 分钟延到 10 分钟，均方位移怎么变？: Extend the recording from 2 to 10 minutes: how does the mean squared displacement change?
把记录次数拖到 20 次（10 分钟），看均方位移涨多少、折线总路程涨多少: Drag the number of records to 20 (10 minutes) and see how much the mean squared displacement and total zigzag length grow
记录点从 4 个变成 20 个（t 从 120 s 到 600 s）：均方位移: Records go from 4 to 20 points (t from 120 s to 600 s): mean squared displacement 204.9 → 1024.6 μm², exactly 5 times = the ratio of times; the root mean square displacement only grows as √t (about √5 times).
均方位移与时间成正比（⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt，二维投影；属拓展 L3，教材本节没有: Mean squared displacement is proportional to time (⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt, 2D projection; extension L3, no formula in this textbook section), so the root mean square displacement grows only as √t, while the zigzag length grows as t; the three quantities must not be mixed up.
⟨r²⟩ ∝ t：时间 5 倍，均方位移就 5 倍。: ⟨r²⟩ ∝ t: 5 times the time gives 5 times the mean squared displacement.
均方根位移 √⟨r²⟩ ∝ √t，只长到约 √5 倍。: Root mean square displacement √⟨r²⟩ ∝ √t, only about √5 times larger.
折线总路程 L ∝ t，跟时间同倍长——路程长不等于「走得远」。: Total zigzag length L ∝ t grows in step with time; a long path doesn't mean "going far".
去掉这一步：「折线越长＝扩散越快」（A7.6）和 ⟨r²⟩ 与 √⟨r²⟩ 混比: Skip this step and neither "longer zigzag = faster diffusion" (A7.6) nor confusing ⟨r²⟩ with √⟨r²⟩ (A7.11) can be prevented.
常考：⟨r²⟩ 与 t 成正比、均方根位移与 √t 成正比；路程与 t 成正比。: Often tested: ⟨r²⟩ is proportional to t, root mean square displacement to √t; path length is proportional to t.
换一颗更小的炭粒，运动是更明显还是更不明显？: With a smaller carbon particle, is the motion more or less pronounced?
把「微粒半径」从 0.5 μm 拖到 0.2 μm：折线整体放大，视窗里撞上来的: Drag "Particle radius" from 0.5 μm to 0.2 μm: the zigzag grows overall and the molecules hitting it in the window thin out
Mean squared displacement 512.3 → 1280.7 μm² (2.5 times = 0.5 / 0.2); impacts fall from 3.86 × 10¹⁵ to 6.17 × 10¹⁴, and the relative fluctuation in impacts rises from 1.61 × 10⁻⁸ to 4.03 × 10⁻⁸. Conversely, drag the radius to 1.0 μm and the mean squared displacement is only 256.1 μm², the zigzag shrinking into a small tangle.
教材 p.4：微粒越小，某一瞬间跟它相撞的液体分子数越少，撞击作用的不平衡性就表: Textbook p.4: the smaller the particle, the fewer liquid molecules hit it at any instant and the more pronounced the imbalance of impacts; also, the smaller the particle, the smaller its mass and the more easily its motion changes, so Brownian motion is more pronounced. The textbook's counterexample: when the particle is very large, impacts from all directions nearly balance and Brownian motion is hard to observe.
A2.6、A5.3（教材 p.4）、B2.1 第 7、8 条、B2.2 表 1: A2.6, A5.3 (textbook p.4), B2.1 items 7, 8, B2.2 table 1 ③④ and table 2
撞击数 N ∝ r²（示意）：3.86 × 10¹⁵ → 6.17 × 10¹⁴: Number of impacts N ∝ r² (schematic): 3.86 × 10¹⁵ → 6.17 × 10¹⁴; the smaller the particle, the fewer hits in a time window.
相对涨落 δ = 1/√N ∝ 1/r：越小越不平衡（1.61 × 10⁻⁸ →: Relative fluctuation δ = 1/√N ∝ 1/r: smaller means more unbalanced (1.61 × 10⁻⁸ → 4.03 × 10⁻⁸, exactly 2.5 times = 0.5 / 0.2).
质量 ∝ r³：同样的净力，微粒越小加速度越大，运动状态越容易被改变。: Mass ∝ r³: for the same net force, a smaller particle accelerates more and its motion changes more easily.
去掉这一步：「越小越明显」会被记成「越小越慢」，教材那个「微粒很大就看不见」的反: Skip this step and "smaller is more pronounced" gets remembered as "smaller is slower", and the textbook's counterexample "too large to see" doesn't stick.
常考：悬浮微粒越小，布朗运动越明显；微粒很大时各方向撞击接近平衡，很难观察到（教: Often tested: the smaller the suspended particle, the more pronounced the Brownian motion; when the particle is very large, impacts nearly balance and it is hard to observe (textbook p.4).
把悬浊液从 20 ℃ 加热到 100 ℃，运动变化有多大？: Heat the suspension from 20 ℃ to 100 ℃: how much does the motion change?
把「温度」从 293 K 拖到 373 K（20 ℃ → 100 ℃），看均方位: Drag "Temperature" from 293 K to 373 K (20 ℃ → 100 ℃) and see how many times the mean squared displacement grows
均方位移 512.3 → 2346.6 μm²（4.5807 倍）；水的粘度从: Mean squared displacement 512.3 → 2346.6 μm² (4.5807 times); water viscosity falls from 1.005 to 0.279 mPa·s, diffusion coefficient 0.427 → 1.956 μm²·s⁻¹. Same particle, same random numbers: the zigzag keeps its direction point by point, just stretched out overall.
教材 p.3 的演示「改变悬浊液的温度。重复上述操作」给出结论：温度越高，小炭粒: The textbook p.3 demonstration "change the temperature of the suspension and repeat" concludes: the higher the temperature, the more pronounced the carbon particles' motion; p.4 "temperature is a measure of how vigorous molecular thermal motion is". Quantitatively (extension), liquid viscosity falls with temperature and viscous drag decreases, so D ∝ T/η(T) grows 4.5807 times, far more than the 1.2730 times from T alone. Illustrative: this lesson takes the temperature to 100 ℃ only to draw the trend to the end; a real suspension would boil and convect at 100 ℃, and no steady Brownian motion would be seen under the microscope.
A2.5、A5.2（教材 p.3–4）、B2.1 第 0、1 条、B2.2 表: A2.5, A5.2 (textbook pp.3–4), B2.1 items 0, 1, B2.2 table 1 ②
温度越高，分子无规则运动越剧烈，撞微粒撞得更凶。: The higher the temperature, the more vigorous the random motion of molecules and the harder they hit the particle.
液体粘度随温度下降（1.005 → 0.279 mPa·s，掉到 1/3.598: Liquid viscosity falls with temperature (1.005 → 0.279 mPa·s, down to 1/3.5982), viscous drag drops, and the same impact fluctuations push the particle farther.
两条合起来，均方位移涨 4.5807 倍——比只看 T 的 1.2730 倍强得: Together the two raise the mean squared displacement 4.5807 times, far more than the 1.2730 times from T alone.
去掉这一步：会把「越热越剧烈」当成一句背下来的话，甚至判反（A7.3）。: Skip this step and "hotter is more vigorous" becomes a memorized phrase, or even gets reversed (A7.3).
常考：温度越高布朗运动越明显；温度是分子热运动剧烈程度的标志（教材 p.4）。: Often tested: the higher the temperature, the more pronounced the Brownian motion; temperature is a measure of how vigorous molecular thermal motion is (textbook p.4).
微粒为什么一会儿往这边、一会儿往那边？: Why does the particle go this way one moment and that way the next?
点一下放大视窗里的炭粒，停在这一瞬间看四面撞来的分子: Click the carbon particle in the magnified window and freeze this instant to see molecules hitting it from all sides
视窗里炭粒四周的撞击箭头疏密不均：这一瞬间左边密、下一瞬间右边密，合力箭头的方向: In the window the impact arrows around the particle are unevenly spread: denser on the left one instant, on the right the next, and the net-force arrow swings around with them; about 3.86 × 10¹⁵ molecules hit it per millisecond (schematic), and the relative fluctuation in impacts is only 1.61 × 10⁻⁸, but it is never zero. The jagged line in the window is the path it really took in 30 s; the corresponding stretch on the graph paper is just one straight segment.
教材 p.4（图 1.1-5）：液体分子不停地做无规则运动，不断地撞击微粒；某一: Textbook p.4 (Fig. 1.1-5): liquid molecules move randomly and ceaselessly and keep hitting the particle; at one instant the impacts are stronger from one direction, at the next from another, and this causes the particle's random motion. The random motion of suspended particles isn't the motion of molecules, but it indirectly reflects the randomness of liquid molecular motion.
A2.4、A4.3、A5.1、A5.8（教材 p.4 图 1.1-5 与旁注）: A2.4, A4.3, A5.1, A5.8 (textbook p.4 Fig. 1.1-5 and margin note)
撞击极密（示意：每毫秒约 3.86 × 10¹⁵ 次），不平衡极其微小（相对涨落: Impacts are extremely frequent (schematic: about 3.86 × 10¹⁵ per millisecond) and the imbalance extremely small (relative fluctuation 1.61 × 10⁻⁸), but the net force is never zero.
合力方向一直在变：这一瞬间偏左、下一瞬间偏右，所以微粒东一步西一步。: The direction of the net force keeps changing: left one instant, right the next, so the particle steps one way then another.
窗里能看到：30 s 内它走过的路是密密麻麻的锯齿——折线上那两个记录点之间的「: In the window you can see that its path over 30 s is a dense jagged line; the "straight line" between two recorded points on the zigzag is just what wasn't recorded.
去掉这一步：布朗运动变成「凭空乱动」，教材说的「间接证据」也就没有着落了。: Skip this step and Brownian motion becomes "random motion out of nowhere", and the textbook's "indirect evidence" has nothing to rest on.
常考：布朗运动的成因是液体分子对微粒撞击的不平衡；它间接反映液体分子的无规则运动: Often tested: Brownian motion is caused by the imbalance of impacts from liquid molecules on the particle; it indirectly reflects the random motion of liquid molecules.
换一颗微粒再测一遍，均方位移会变吗？: Measure a different particle: does the mean squared displacement change?
把「哪颗微粒」从①拨到②：坐标纸上换成第二颗微粒的折线: Switch "Which particle" from ① to ②: the graph paper shows the second particle's zigzag
净位移从 16.50 变成 29.26 μm、路程从 64.8 变成 67.2: Net displacement goes from 16.50 to 29.26 μm and path length from 64.8 to 67.2 μm, yet the mean squared displacement is still 512.3 μm², unchanged.
布朗运动是统计规律：单次结果涨落很大，只有大量微粒（或很多次）平均起来，⟨r²⟩: Brownian motion follows a statistical law: single results fluctuate widely, and only averaging over many particles (or many runs) makes ⟨r²⟩ stable. Textbook Fig. 1.1-4 draws three particles with three completely different zigzags for exactly this reason.
同一颗微粒、同一工况，每次读数逐位相同（带种子的随机数，不是每次重掷骰子）。: Same particle, same conditions: every reading matches digit for digit (seeded random numbers, not a fresh roll of the dice each time).
换一颗微粒：净位移 16.50 → 29.26 μm，差了近一倍——这是单次结果: Change the particle: net displacement 16.50 → 29.26 μm, nearly double; that's the fluctuation of a single result.
⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt 是统计平均，不随单次结果变：512.3 μm² 一直在那儿: ⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt is a statistical average and doesn't change with single results: 512.3 μm² stays put.
去掉这一步：学生会拿一次读数下结论（A7.12），也读不懂教材为什么画三颗微粒。: Skip this step and students draw conclusions from a single reading (A7.12) and can't see why the textbook draws three particles.
常考：单次观测的位移有偶然性；大量微粒才显出统计规律。: Often tested: displacement from a single observation is random; only many particles reveal the statistical law.
一杯静水里滴一滴墨，为什么过一会儿周围都变黑了？: Drop some ink into a glass of still water: why does everything around it turn dark after a while?
把「观察时长」从 300 s 拖到 1800 s（30 分钟），看墨迹展宽多少: Drag "Observation time" from 300 s to 1800 s (30 minutes) and see how much the ink trace widens
墨迹从中间一条窄线向两侧展开：扩散宽度 1.432 mm，中心浓度从初始的 10: The ink spreads from a narrow line in the middle to both sides: diffusion width 1.432 mm, center concentration falls from an initial 100 % (initial spot width 0.5 mm) to 34.9 %; the dashed line on the profile board is a 100 ℃ comparison at the same moment (2.915 mm, 17.2 %, schematic).
教材 p.3：扩散现象并不是外界作用（例如对流、重力作用等）引起的，也不是化学反: Textbook p.3: diffusion is not caused by external action (such as convection or gravity) and is not a chemical reaction; it arises from the random motion of molecules and is one piece of evidence that molecules move randomly and ceaselessly; p.4 "the higher the temperature, the faster the diffusion"; at the same moment, the diffusion width at 100 ℃ is nearly twice that at 20 ℃, and the peak is only half as high: the area is conserved, so a lower peak means a wider spread.
A2.1、A2.2（教材 p.3–4）、A6.3（画法示意）、B2.1 第 9: A2.1, A2.2 (textbook pp.3–4), A6.3 (drawing illustrative), B2.1 item 9, B2.2 table 2
扩散靠分子热运动，不需要搅拌，也不是化学反应。: Diffusion relies on molecular thermal motion; it needs no stirring and isn't a chemical reaction.
峰变矮、曲线变宽是同一件事：浓度曲线的面积守恒。: A lower peak and a wider curve are the same thing: the area under the concentration curve is conserved.
温度升高扩散更快：墨水的扩散系数 500.00 → 2290.34 μm²·s⁻: Higher temperature, faster diffusion: the ink's diffusion coefficient 500.00 → 2290.34 μm²·s⁻¹ (20 ℃ → 100 ℃).
去掉这一步：学生会把扩散当成「外力推动」或「化学反应」（A7.7），也接不上「两: Skip this step and students see diffusion as "pushed by external force" or "a chemical reaction" (A7.7), and can't connect "two phenomena, one root cause".
常考：扩散是分子无规则运动的证据；温度越高扩散越快；不需要外力。: Often tested: diffusion is evidence of the random motion of molecules; the higher the temperature, the faster the diffusion; no external force is needed.
面积守恒：峰矮了就宽: Area conserved: lower peak, wider spread
想让这颗炭粒的均方位移达到 2000 μm² 以上，怎么调？: How would you get this carbon particle's mean squared displacement above 2000 μm²?
把均方位移调到 2000 μm² 以上并稳住：升温，或者换更小的微粒: Bring the mean squared displacement above 2000 μm² and hold it: raise the temperature, or use a smaller particle
均方位移 ≥ 2000 μm² 并保持 12 s：目标条变绿、达标胶囊亮，3D: Mean squared displacement ≥ 2000 μm² held for 12 s: the goal bar turns green, the pass badge lights up, and the plotted points on the graph paper in 3D enlarge accordingly.
温度升高或换更小的微粒，都能让 ⟨r²⟩ 变大：20 ℃、0.5 μm 是 51: Raising the temperature or using a smaller particle both increase ⟨r²⟩: 512.3 μm² at 20 ℃ and 0.5 μm, 2346.6 μm² for the same particle at 100 ℃; reducing the radius from 0.5 to 0.2 μm gives 1280.7 μm². The textbook's conclusion "the higher the temperature and the smaller the particle, the more pronounced the motion" becomes an achievable goal here.
A2.5、A2.6、B2.2 表 1、B2.4 考核判据: A2.5, A2.6, B2.2 table 1, B2.4 assessment criterion
两条路都行：升温，或换更小的微粒——都让 ⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt 变大。: Either path works: raise the temperature, or use a smaller particle; both make ⟨r²⟩ = 4Dt larger.
判据是统计量 ⟨r²⟩ 的期望值，不是屏上这一条随机轨迹的 r²（单条轨迹涨落很: The criterion is the expected value of the statistic ⟨r²⟩, not the r² of the single random trajectory on screen (a single trajectory fluctuates a lot).
只加记录次数不够：次数上限 20 次（10 分钟）也只有 1024.6 μm²。: Just adding records isn't enough: even the maximum of 20 records (10 minutes) gives only 1024.6 μm².
没有新结论：把前面「越大越明显」的两条路用一次，就是考核。: No new conclusion: using one of the earlier "larger is more pronounced" paths once is the assessment.
综合：温度、微粒大小对布朗运动的影响，以及「单次 ≠ 统计」。: Synthesis: the effects of temperature and particle size on Brownian motion, and "single ≠ statistical".
升温，或者换更小的微粒——两条路都行（别只看一条轨迹的净位移）: Raise the temperature or use a smaller particle; either works (don't just look at one trajectory's net displacement)
1 滴用水稀释的墨汁: 1 drop of ink diluted with water
每隔 30 s 记一个位置（教材 p.4）: A position recorded every 30 s (textbook p.4)
静水 · 一滴墨: Still water · a drop of ink
观察条件：温度 · 微粒大小 · 记录次数: Observation conditions: temperature · particle size · number of records
回到参考工况：20 ℃ · 0.5 μm · 记 10 次（300 s）: Back to the reference case: 20 ℃ · 0.5 μm · 10 records (300 s)
显微镜下看到的「布朗运动」，运动的是: In the "Brownian motion" seen under a microscope, what moves is
教材 p.4 旁注：悬浮微粒的无规则运动并不是分子的运动，但可以间接反映液体分子: Textbook p.4 margin note: the random motion of suspended particles isn't the motion of molecules, but it indirectly reflects the randomness of liquid molecular motion.
向一锅水中撒一点胡椒粉，加热时发现胡椒粉在水中翻滚。这说明温度越高布朗运动越剧烈: Sprinkle a little pepper into a pot of water and heat it; the pepper tumbles in the water. Does this show that Brownian motion is more vigorous at higher temperature?
说明，温度越高越剧烈: Yes, the higher the temperature, the more vigorous
不能说明，那是加热引起的水流（对流）: No, that's water flow caused by heating (convection)
不能说明，因为胡椒粉太大看不见: No, because pepper is too large to see
说明，但也说明分子有大有小: Yes, and it also shows molecules come in different sizes
翻滚是对流（外界作用），不是分子撞击造成的不平衡；布朗运动要在高倍显微镜下看悬浮: The tumbling is convection (an external action), not an imbalance of molecular impacts; Brownian motion is seen in suspended particles under a high-power microscope (textbook p.6 question 3 (3)).
在显微镜下可以观察到煤油中小粒灰尘的布朗运动，这说明: Brownian motion of small dust particles in kerosene can be observed under a microscope. This shows that
煤油分子之间有间隙: There are gaps between kerosene molecules
灰尘分子比煤油分子小: Dust molecules are smaller than kerosene molecules
任何液体都行；被证明的是液体（煤油）分子的无规则运动，不是灰尘分子（教材 p.6: Any liquid works; what's demonstrated is the random motion of the liquid's (kerosene's) molecules, not the dust's (textbook p.6 question 3 (4)).
把每隔 30 s 记录的炭粒位置依次连成折线，这条折线: The carbon particle's positions recorded every 30 s are joined in order into a zigzag. This zigzag
是真实路径的放大: Is an enlargement of the real path
只是采样连线，两点之间炭粒仍在乱走: Only joins samples; between two points the particle keeps wandering
说明水分子在短时间内的运动是规则的: Shows that water molecules move regularly over short times
教材 p.4：就是在 30 s 内，微粒的运动也是极不规则的——两点之间的「直线: Textbook p.4: even within 30 s, the particle's motion is extremely irregular; the "straight line" between two points is just what wasn't recorded (textbook p.6 question 4).
悬浮微粒越小，布朗运动越明显，原因是: The smaller the suspended particle, the more pronounced the Brownian motion, because
微粒越小，液体分子撞得越狠: Liquid molecules hit smaller particles harder
某一瞬间撞它的分子数越少、撞击越不平衡，而且质量越小越容易被改变运动状态: Fewer molecules hit it at any instant so impacts are more unbalanced, and its smaller mass makes its motion easier to change
微粒越小，水的粘度越小: Smaller particles make water less viscous
教材 p.4 给了这两条理由（撞击数少 + 质量小）；温度与粘度是另一回事。: Textbook p.4 gives these two reasons (fewer impacts + smaller mass); temperature and viscosity are a separate matter.
分子动理论的基本内容是: The basic content of kinetic molecular theory is
物体由大量分子组成，分子永不停息地做无规则运动，分子之间有相互作用力: Matter is made of many molecules, molecules move randomly and ceaselessly, and there are forces between molecules
分子之间只有引力: There is only attraction between molecules
温度越高分子越大: Molecules get bigger at higher temperature
教材 p.6 原话三条一条不能少，术语是「分子动理论」（A2.7）。: None of the textbook p.6's three statements can be left out; the term is "kinetic molecular theory" (A2.7).
看清显微镜下的小炭粒怎么乱走，再用一句话说清「为什么越热、越小越明显」。: See how the small carbon particles wander under the microscope, then explain in one sentence why hotter and smaller means more pronounced.
